newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA PARLIAMENT RATIFIES TREATY WITH HUNGARY.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA PARLIAMENT RATIFIES TREATY WITH HUNGARY.

text.p: Romanian parliament's upper Senate on Thursday ratified a recently signed treaty with Hungary, which is expected to help the ex-communist neighbours to join NATO and the European Union.

Members of the 143-strong Senate voted by 87 to 13, with three abstentions, to ratify the long-delayed accord, which settles old border rifts and provides guarantees for the rights of the large ethnic Hungarian minority in Romania.

Ignoring nationalist opposition in both countries, Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn flew to the western city of Timisoara, on the border with Hungary, on September 16, to sign the treaty with his Romanian counterpart Nicolae Vacaroiu.

Vacaroiu's leftist Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) hopes to push the treaty through the lower Chamber of Deputies by the end of next week, when parliament adjourns for electioneering ahead of the November 3 polls, which coincide with presidental elections.
Ethnic Hungarians leaders say the treaty should help their quest for greater language and education rights for the 1.6 million Hungarians in Romania's central Transylvania region.
But Romanian nationalists oppose it, saying it jeopardises "the country's national sovereignty and integrity".
The pact, agreed under Western pressure, is vital for both countries' ambitions to join the EU and NATO.

Politicians from the nationalist Romanian National Unity Party (PUNR) voted against ratifying the treaty on Thursday, while their colleagues from the Hungarian Democratic Union of Romania (UDMR) declined to say which way their vote had gone.
"Without being against it (the treaty), I cannot support it either," UDMR senator Karoly Szabo said, without saying whether he had abstained or voted against.
